dataset.title: Proteomic profiling of young and old mice in the bleomycin model

findings.message: The bundle holds 206774 where the producer reported 206775 (results.txt: All target PSMs with q-value <= 0.01 (pxreprise:DEF-PSM-1PCT v1)). Both numbers are kept; treat the producer's as canonical until the difference is explained.

no SDRF says which sample is in which channel (no curated design and no deposited SDRF); PXReprise's default design makes each file its own plex and each channel that shows a sample its own sample (marked empty, holding none: 128N in 8 file(s)); the reporter values compare nothing until a design is curated (QuantProject 079)

No SDRF was found for this dataset, so each channel's sample is the sample its search's TmtDesign.txt names (its `Sample Name`), with nothing else known about it. There is no sample metadata: treat every sample as unannotated.

Some modifications on peptides shared between proteins were not written to ptm_sites for one or more of those proteins, because the peptide could not be located in that protein's sequence and the producer's residue spans cannot be paired with its accessions. Of the (PSM, protein) pairs affected: 1643 named a protein that does not contain the stored peptide -- typically a PSM ambiguous between peptide sequences (level 4 or 5), where this protein carries a different candidate than the first, which is the one stored. Sites on the other proteins of the same PSMs are written. Counts are in bundle.json under protein_databases.

3 modification(s) could not be mapped to a UNIMOD accession or a mass, and are carried in ProForma as [Info:...] tags: UniProt:5-glutamyl histamine on Q, UniProt:Omega-hydroxyceramide glutamate ester on Q, UniProt:S-(15-deoxy-Delta12,14-prostaglandin J2-9-yl)cysteine on C. Their ptm_sites rows exist and carry modification_name, with modification null, so a query by name finds them and a query by UNIMOD accession will not.

8 channel(s) of the search's TmtDesign.txt are not study samples: `Sample Type` empty: `PXD026222:20180720_lung_3_fraction_1:TMT128N`, `PXD026222:20180720_lung_3_fraction_2:TMT128N`, `PXD026222:20180720_lung_3_fraction_3:TMT128N`, `PXD026222:20180720_lung_3_fraction_4:TMT128N`, `PXD026222:20180720_lung_3_fraction_5:TMT128N` and 3 more. Their values measure that reference, not a sample of the question. The design is copied in `sources/`, and each assay keeps its `Sample Type` (`assays.design_sample_type`). A channel marked `empty` had no sample put in it: unless the SDRF names one for it, its assay has no `sample_id`, and its values are kept as measured (isotope spill-over from a neighbouring channel, PXReprise 098), so a count of samples never counts it and a median across a run's channels must leave it out.

PTM site occupancy was not stored: this is a TMT dataset, and MetaMorpheus computes intensity occupancy for label-free searches only; its count occupancy is per file, repeated on every channel (QuantProject DEF-OCC-INT). `ptm_stoichiometry` has no rows here because of that, not because no site was modified.

No per-run `metrics` row from results.txt for `psms_1pct` (24 of 24 runs), `peptides` (24 of 24 runs), `protein_groups` (24 of 24 runs). These counts were not written, which is not a count of zero. The search task sets `WriteIndividualFiles = false`, and MetaMorpheus writes results.txt's per-file PSM, peptide and protein-group lines only when it is true (before 1.1.14, MetaMorpheus #2955, its per-file precursor and MS2 lines too). PXReprise's QC payload counts each run's share of the whole search's 1% set instead, a different number (the FDR is the whole search's, not recomputed on each file), under names of its own (`source = 'qc_payload.json'`): `psms_1pct_whole_search` for 24 of the 24 runs, `peptides_1pct_whole_search` for 24 of the 24 runs, `protein_groups_1pct_whole_search` for none of them.

dataset.summary: PXD026222 is a DDA isobaric dataset (Mus musculus) with 24 runs, 256 samples and no enrichment step (whole proteome). It was reanalysed with MetaMorpheus 1.1.14. At 1% FDR the search reports 206,774 PSMs and 5,673 protein groups; 46,555 peptidoforms pass 1% on its q-value and notch q-value, and the repository holds 105,562 PTM sites for it. 6 open warnings about it are recorded.

organisms_are: `organisms` is the organism of the protein DATABASE the search used, not a statement about the samples. Sample annotation, where any exists, is in the catalog's `samples` and `sample_characteristics` tables.
